newsitem.title: USA: LatAm economic growth to accelerate in '97 -report.
newsitem.headline: LatAm economic growth to accelerate in '97 -report.

text.p: Economic growth rates for many Latin American nations in 1997 should exceed the levels of the past two years, according to a Price Waterhouse report.

"The macroeconomic fundamentals have improved steadily during the past two years in several larger economies," said Antonio Villamil, senior adviser to the Price Waterhouse Latin American Business Center.
The report said a decline in inflationary pressures, an increase in exports and more foreign exchange-rate stability over the past year should spur growth in 1997.

Specifically, the report projected improved Gross Domestic Product growth in Argentina, to 4.0 percent in 1997 from an estimated 2.5 percent in 1996, and in Brazil, to 4.5 percent this year from an estimated 3.0 percent last year, according to Villamil.

The report said output growth in Mexico probably will slow to 4.0 percent in 1997 from a projected 4.5 percent the year before, but that would still represent a strong economic performance, Villamil said.
The Price Waterhouse report highlighted a few stumbling blocks that may limit the pace of economic activity going forward.
"Regional economic growth continues to be limited by resistance to structural reforms, macroeconomic imbalances and inconsistent application of economic and fiscal policies," it said.
